name: Mui Ne
provinceNote: This shore is now in Lam Dong. Older pages and Decision 1772/QĐ-TTg still say Binh Thuan. Resolution 202/2025/QH15 of 12 Jun 2025 is the merger, and Resolution 1671/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 Jun 2025 creates the new Mui Ne ward from the old Ham Tien ward, the old Mui Ne ward, and Thien Nghiep. The older ward is about 25,000 people, and 24,275 in 1999 on 35.41 km². The merged ward is 50,166 people on 31 Dec 2024 across 118.59 km².

summary: A beach resort strip near Phan Thiet, known for kitesurfing and red and white sand dunes. Kitesurf or relax on the sand, ride to the red dunes at sunset and the white dunes at dawn, and eat seafood by the fishing village. A good beach break for active travellers and families.

seoTitle: Mui Ne travel guide — red and white dunes, the kite
seoDescription: Sleep on the Ham Tien sand for the kite. Ride the red dunes at sunset and the white dunes at Bàu Trắng at dawn, then eat on the sea wall by the fishing village.
intro: A kite stands over the Ham Tien surf, and the day runs out to the red dunes and back to the white field at Bàu Trắng. Sleep on that sand when the wind is why you came. The built beach is Rang, in Ham Tien, and visitors call it Mui Ne Beach. The fishing ward, with Ganh and Suoi Nuoc, sits farther along the bay.

Give the morning to the harbor if you are not leaving for the white dunes. The boats unload just after dawn, then cards and coffee once the catch is on the sand. A first kite lesson fits the gentler morning wind. The stronger thermal wind is 11:00–16:00, with IKO instructors on the main beach strip. Kite season is October to April, the coast window is November to April, and the breeze is also given as year-round.

The red dunes are the late ride. Walk the orange slope and sandboard at sunset. Đồi cát bay sits in Mui Ne ward, Phan Thiet, about 22 km from the city center, a field of about 36.8 ha, and it is also just outside town. Since 2016 the field has been with the provincial youth outdoor center. The white field is Bàu Trắng, in Hoa Thang, the symbol of the national tourism zone: steep 30-metre dunes, a lotus lake, and a visit at 5:00–7:00. The drive is 25 km, and also a short ride from the main beach strip. Set the alarm for 4:30 if an ATV at sunrise is the plan. Midday sand on that field is scorching.

Dinner is the sea wall by the fishing village, the grills called bờ kè. You pick from the tanks: fresh oysters, lemongrass clams, garlic scallops, grilled prawns, crispy fish, and chili stuffed squid, with beer. Nguyễn Đình Chiểu is the restaurant road from the center of Mui Ne toward the village, and Tuyên Quang is the other street. On the way in from Phan Thiet, the Po Sah Inu towers stand on Ba Nai Hill in Phu Hai, about 7 km northeast of the city center: three brick towers, called 1,200-year-old Hoa Lai national monuments, the main tower holding a Linga-Yoni altar. Between the strip and the dunes, the fairy stream is a shallow walk, Suối Tiên and also Suối Hồng. Take your shoes off. It is ankle-deep, red clay and limestone on one side, not a canyon. A coconut at a rest stop is named.
gettingAround: The strip is a road, not a grid you walk. A motorbike covers the dunes and the coast. Nguyễn Đình Chiểu (ĐT 706) and Võ Nguyên Giáp (ĐT 706B) tie Mui Ne to Phan Thiet. Võ Nguyên Giáp and provincial roads 715, 716, and 716B run along the north edge of the tourism zone.

From Ho Chi Minh City the coast is about four hours by road, and Phan Thiet is a four-hour taxi, bus, or car ride. The same journey is also given as Phan Thiet at four hours with Mui Ne 25 km farther. Mui Ne is about 22 km from Phan Thiet ward. The flying dunes are about 22 km from the city center. The 25 km is the farther figure from Phan Thiet, and the 22 km is the ward and the dunes.

The train ends at Phan Thiet station, not in the fishing ward. From 11 Sep 2026 through 30 Dec 2026, SPT2 and SPT1 run Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. SPT2 leaves Saigon at 6:45 and reaches Phan Thiet at 10:42. SPT1 leaves Phan Thiet at 13:30 and reaches Saigon at 17:46. A 2023 timetable has SPT2 arriving Phan Thiet at 10:40, and SPT1 leaving Phan Thiet at 13:10 and reaching Saigon at 17:35. Mui Ne is also an open-tour stop.

No civil passenger airport is open on this coast. There is no airport in Phan Thiet, so the flight is to Ho Chi Minh City, Nha Trang, or Da Lat, then a bus or a train. The civil-terminal groundbreaking at Phan Thiet was 27 Apr 2026. The military side was already operating. A 2018 plan names Tan Son Nhat and Cam Ranh as the air links, and a Phan Thiet airport only after 2025.

stayAreas.name: Ham Tien sand
stayAreas.summary: Medium and small resorts sit in the Mui Ne–Ham Tien sea zone, about 340 ha on the 2018 plan. Smaller rooms are in the ward centers and the fishing village.

eat: Dinner is the sea wall by the fishing village. The local list starts with lẩu thả, mực một nắng, and the grill you pick from the tanks. Nguyễn Đình Chiểu and Tuyên Quang are the restaurant roads.
Twenty-eight plates are named, from the Mui Ne table, the sea-wall grill, and the Binh Thuan coast menu.
interestsBody: Eat on the sea wall, then along Nguyễn Đình Chiểu. The kite wind is on the Ham Tien sand. The red slope is the sunset picture. Bàu Trắng is the dawn picture. The fairy stream is the shallow walk between the strip and the dunes.
The night sits in the Mui Ne–Ham Tien sea zone. Po Sah Inu is the Cham stop on the road in from Phan Thiet, not a sight inside the fishing ward.

blocks.heading: Fishing-village market
paragraphs: Just after dawn the boats unload at the fishing village and the bargaining is on the sand. Cards and coffee follow once the catch is in. By noon that market is over. The sea wall beside it is dinner, not this market.
On Nguyễn Đình Chiểu, the food court includes a wine shop and a handmade chocolate shop, with the foreign kitchens.

body: The lesson beach is the Ham Tien sand. The wind is gentler in the morning and stronger in the late afternoon. The thermal wind is 11:00–16:00, October to April, with IKO instructors. The breeze is also given as year-round, and the coast window as November to April.

blocks.heading: Dawn boats
paragraphs: Just after dawn, stand out of the way at the fishing-village market while the boats unload. Cards and coffee follow once the catch is on the sand. Arrive at noon and that market is already over.

blocks.heading: Sea wall after dark
paragraphs: The evening area is the sea wall by the fishing village. You pick seafood from the tanks and eat on the wall: oysters, lemongrass clams, garlic scallops, grilled prawns, crispy fish, and chili stuffed squid, with beer.

blocks.heading: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu
paragraphs: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu runs from the center of Mui Ne toward the fishing village, and Tuyên Quang is the other street, with rooms from cozy to cosmopolitan. Night activity sits in the Mui Ne sea zone.

blocks.heading: Red slope at the end of the day
paragraphs: Đồi cát bay is the orange field. Go at sunset for the walk and the sandboard. The field is about 36.8 ha in Mui Ne ward, Phan Thiet, about 22 km from the city center, and also just outside town. Since 2016 it has been with the provincial youth outdoor center. The 22 km figure is from the city center, not from a resort gate.

blocks.heading: White field and the lake
paragraphs: Bàu Trắng is in Hoa Thang, Bac Binh, inside the national tourism zone, and it is called the symbol of Mui Ne. Bàu Sen is named with it for protection and is not given a separate visit. The dunes are steep and 30 metres, with a lotus lake. Be there from 5:00 to 7:00. The drive is 25 km, and also a short drive from the main beach strip.

blocks.heading: A shallow walk inland
paragraphs: The fairy stream sits under the Mui Ne sand hills. It is Suối Tiên, and also Suối Hồng. You take your shoes off and walk upstream in ankle-deep water, red clay and limestone on one side. A coconut at a rest stop is named.

blocks.heading: Tower on the way in
paragraphs: Tháp Pô Sah Inư stands on Ba Nai Hill in Phu Hai, about 7 km northeast of Phan Thiet center, on the road between the city and the strip. The three brick towers are called 1,200-year-old Hoa Lai national monuments. The main tower holds a Linga-Yoni altar. The ticket is 7,000–15,000 VND, with adult and child not split. Hours are 7:00–17:00 and 7:00–18:00. Addresses are Km9 Nguyễn Thông, Phường Phú Thuỷ, Lâm Đồng, and Phường Phú Hài, Phan Thiết, Bình Thuận. The morning of 2 Oct 2024 was Katê at these towers.

faqs.q: How do you get here from Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: The road is about four hours. Phan Thiet is also given as four hours, with Mui Ne 25 km farther, and Mui Ne is about 22 km from Phan Thiet ward. The train ends at Phan Thiet station. From 11 Sep 2026 through 30 Dec 2026, SPT2 and SPT1 run Friday, Saturday, and Sunday: Saigon 6:45, Phan Thiet 10:42, and back 13:30 to 17:46. A 2023 timetable has 10:40 and a return at 13:10–17:35.

The morning wind is gentler and the late afternoon is stronger. Kite winds are October to April, with the beach window at 11:00–16:00. The breeze is also given as year-round, and the coast window as November to April.

The red dunes are about 22 km from the Phan Thiet city center, and just outside town. The white dunes are a 25 km drive, and a short drive from the main beach strip. Be at Bàu Trắng from 5:00 to 7:00.

season.label: Dry wind months
season.note: November to April is dry, sunny, and windy, the time for kites and dune slides. Kite winds are also given as October to April, with the beach window at 11:00–16:00, and the breeze and the water as warm year-round. December to April is called the tourist season, with an average of 27°C. Warm sun is also given all year, with daily temperatures around 27°C. On the white dunes, go at 5:00–7:00. Midday sand is scorching.
